title: Building a rectangle from a side of three and a diagonal of seven
description: A rectangle with one side of three centimetres and a diagonal of seven centimetres is built in the same order as before. The base goes first, then a perpendicular, then a compass arc for the diagonal.
teaching_notes: One idea: draw the known side as the base, raise a perpendicular at one end, and cut it with an arc whose centre is the other end of the base and whose opening is the diagonal. Watch for students who forget that the arc needs the diagonal to be longer than the base.

video_script.why: A learner repeats the base, perpendicular and arc method once more, this time with a short side and a long diagonal, and checks the figure.
video_script.substitution: the rectangle ABCD with the base AB of three centimetres and the diagonal BD of seven centimetres
video_script.anchor: a rough rectangle ABCD with the base AB marked 3 cm and the diagonal BD marked 7 cm
video_script.payoff_line: The rectangle is ready. Its sides are three centimetres and about six point three centimetres, and its diagonal is seven centimetres.

final_answer.value: rectangle ABCD with AB = DC = 3 cm, AD = BC about 6.3 cm and diagonal BD = 7 cm
final_answer.spoken: a rectangle with sides three centimetres and about six point three centimetres, and a diagonal of seven centimetres

maths_rules: the base AB is 3 cm and the line at A is perpendicular to AB
D lies on that line and is 7 cm from B, because the diagonal BD is 7 cm
the other sides AD and BC are equal, about 6.3 cm, since 7 x 7 - 3 x 3 = 40 and the square root of 40 is about 6.3
opposite sides are equal and all angles are 90 degrees
video_script.design: A rough rectangle ABCD stays at the side. The construction is drawn in four steps, and the compass opening of seven centimetres stays visible while the arc is drawn from B.
